correctness.rationale: For each of 12 cube edges, its endpoints and two rhombic-dodecahedron axial-corner edges contribute exactly one plane crossing for a generic normal, as shown by three sign possibilities. Every rhombic edge belongs to exactly one such pair, establishing N_C+N_R=12; replacing the normal by T^T u proves affine-matched pointwise identity. A generic cube central cut has 4 or 6 vertices, hence its rhombic partner has 8 or 6. A Haar great-circle separation probability equals the angle between endpoint rays divided by pi, and summing 24 edges yields P_R(6)=(4/pi) sum_i arcsin(a_i/sqrt(sum a^2))-2 for diagonal T. Maximizing sum arcsin x_i on positive unit octant gives only critical x_i=1/sqrt(3), with boundary value pi/2, and logarithmic Taylor expansion yields coefficient 1/(pi sqrt(2)). Independently checked integer-normal edge crossings and exact symbolic Hessian; no finite sampling was used as proof.
